source_title: UP Politics: Amit Shah Targets Akhilesh Yadav Over 1990 Ayodhya Firing, Sets BJP's Mission 2027 Agenda!
source_excerpt:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party and its chief Akhilesh Yadav during the Uttar Pradesh BJP State Working Committee meeting in Lucknow. Addressing nearly 2,850 party workers and leaders, Shah delivered an approximately 40-minute speech, focusing on the BJP's preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. According to sources, Amit Shah began his address by recalling the events of October 30, 1990, when police opened fire on Ram devotees and kar sevaks in Ayodhya during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, under the government led by Mulayam Singh Yadav. Shah questioned how the Samajwadi Party could seek power in Uttar Pradesh despite those events. He reportedly said that the people would not forgive Akhilesh Yadav and even his next generations for the incident. Shah also asserted that the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh was firmly established and could not be removed, comparing its position to Angad's unshakable foot. He expressed confidence that the BJP would return to power in 2027, just as it did in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections. During his address, Shah also targeted Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav, questioning their electoral performance and claiming that their parties would remain out of power for the next 30 years. He praised Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's leadership, particularly highlighting improvements in law and order, investment opportunities and infrastructure development in the state. Shah also emphasised the importance of party workers, saying that the organisation's strength comes from their dedication and grassroots efforts. BJP leaders present at the meeting expressed confidence in the party's electoral prospects. Senior leader Jagdambika Pal also predicted a strong BJP victory in 2027, crediting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision, Yogi Adityanath's governance and the hard work of party workers. The meeting has effectively set the political tone for the BJP's Mission 2027 campaign.
